_comment: Every number here is enforced in code, never in a prompt. sender.js and messenger.js re-derive all of it themselves, so a bad queue can only be truncated, never obeyed. t18-limits-sanity.test.js pins the ceilings against LinkedIn's real free-account limits.
_invites_comment: LinkedIn enforces roughly 100 connection invitations per WEEK on a free account, and the weekly ceiling is the one that actually gets people restricted. 90 leaves headroom under it. The ramp exists because a brand-new automated sender jumping straight to its cap is the single loudest signal there is.
_dms_comment: DMs go only to people who already accepted, so they are far safer than invites — but they were previously flat 25/day from day one with NO ramp and NO weekly ceiling, i.e. up to 125/week from a cold account. Now ramped and capped like invites.
_pending_comment: A pile of unanswered invites is a top restriction signal, AND it drags trailingAcceptance down until the 25% floor breaker halts sending for a bookkeeping reason rather than a real one. withdraw_pending.js retires them; maxOutstandingInvites stops queueing new ones while the pile is too big.
